Thanks for providing that info! According to the sonarless-mcp documentation, tokens should never be passed through commands or chat. Instead, you'll need to run this command in your terminal, and you'll be prompted to enter the token interactively:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

When prompted, paste your token: `<token>`

This keeps the token secure and out of command histories. After you've added the remote, you can verify it with:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote list
```

Once configured, the remote will be available as `server: "ci"` in the MCP tools, so you can analyze CI results without exposing the token in chat.

Got it! To add your CI SonarQube remote securely, **run this command in your terminal** (the token prompt will be hidden):

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

This will prompt for your token interactively — paste `<token>` there. The token stays in your local sonarless config and never passes through chat.

After that, you'll be able to query the remote server with `server: "ci"` in MCP tool calls, and use commands like `sonarless-mcp remote sync ci` to align your local rules with CI's.
